component.name: Reolink Linux Client
component.summary: Native Linux client for Reolink cameras and NVRs

description.p: A fully native Linux desktop client for Reolink cameras and NVRs — a 1:1 replica of the official Reolink Client. Live grid (1/4/9/16) with hardware-accelerated H.264/H.265 decode, double-click maximize and fullscreen, PTZ, snapshots, manual recording, a color-coded playback timeline, an events inbox, and the full device-settings surface.
Not affiliated with or endorsed by Reolink.

Recordings keep the camera's sound, and HD recordings play correctly again. Playback gets a speaker button. Talk works from pop-out windows too, can be held to talk, shows a microphone level meter, and lets you pick the microphone.

Two-way talk: click the microphone button on a live camera to speak through its speaker, and answering a doorbell starts talk too. Also fixes a doorbell behind an NVR or hub opening the wrong camera when its alert was answered.
Live audio: unmute a live pane or a pop-out window to hear that camera. Only one is audible at a time, and the sound stays continuous on Home Hub cameras that deliver it in bursts.
PTZ and zoom controls only appear on cameras that can use them: pan/tilt-only cameras no longer show zoom buttons that do nothing, and battery cameras without a motor no longer show a PTZ button.
Fixes a Home Hub with a camera that has no battery: start-up took about 20 seconds and the other cameras' live view was broken.
A new Recordings page lists a day's recordings from every camera, filterable by camera, with a download button that shows progress and can save to a folder of your choice.

Smooth live view: a per-pane Smooth button (on by default) shows frames on the camera's clock behind a small adaptive delay of at most 0.3 s, removing the freezes and catch-up skips caused by bursty delivery. The interface now scales with the desktop font size. Live and playback streams stop while the window is hidden in the tray. Timeline clicks snap to nearby recordings, and events show their actual time. Fixes a CPU spin when a Baichuan connection drops, and streams are now torn down cleanly on stop and quit.

First release of this fork. Home Hub support: SD playback over Baichuan where the hub has no HTTP-FLV, and clip export that cuts exact-length clips with audio from a Baichuan replay, plus a Whole recording export. Battery status for every camera behind a hub or NVR, refreshed every minute. A 2-pane stacked live grid, and the grid size and per-camera SD/HD choice remembered across restarts.

Fixes playback failing with a retrying black screen on systems with FFmpeg 8 or newer, playback stopping at every event marker, and a device re-add leaving its header stuck on "connecting". Event playback now starts five seconds before the moment.

Fixes HD streaming on cameras whose firmware doesn't report the main-stream codec (the stream is now probed instead of assumed), fixes false 90-degree rotation of hub-attached cameras, and adds a persisted per-camera Rotate View override.

Synced 4-camera playback on one timeline with per-camera coverage lanes, drag-and-drop camera arrangement in both live view and playback, double-click maximize with an HD toggle, digital zoom in playback panes, honest device error states with automatic recovery for unreachable devices, credential repair from the sidebar, and pre-validated Add Device with inline errors.

Launching the app again now raises the running window instead of starting a second copy, so tray icons no longer pile up. Hardware video decoding works on hosts with VAAPI, cutting CPU use during live view.

System tray with background monitoring, camera offline alerts, event thumbnails and per-camera filtering, detection markers on the playback timeline, clip export, and a weekly recording-schedule editor.
Clicking a detection notification now opens the app and plays that event back; the app version is shown in the nav bar.
The AppImage now runs natively on Wayland (bundles the Qt Wayland platform plugins) instead of falling back to XWayland.
Detection-zone editor, 6-camera live grid, desktop notifications, a nested device tree with icons, event retention cap, and a built-in update checker.
Initial development release: live view, playback, events, and settings.
